B: Hi! Hi, can you hear me okay?
A: Yes. Hello.
B: Hi, sorry, I'm Elira. I think we've just got three minutes, so, erm, I don't really know how this works. Shall I go first?
A: Okay. Go.
B: Okay. So I'm in Walthamstow, in London, and I'm sort of between jobs at the moment. I was an office coordinator at a property management company in Stratford, but they restructured, so I took voluntary redundancy. Now I'm applying for office manager roles and doing a bookkeeping course online. Which is, you know, it's fine. It's a lot of applications.
A: Property management. So you are landlord side.
B: Erm, kind of? We managed blocks for the owners, so I dealt with tenants and contractors and that. Why, are you renting?
A: Yes. In Bletchley, Milton Keynes. When I come there, rent was maybe four hundred fifty. Now same kind of flat is nine hundred, more. For what? Nothing changed. Same carpet.
B: Oh, don't. Honestly, in London it's even worse. We had tenants paying, like, sixteen hundred for a one-bed and the boiler going every winter.
A: Yeah, yeah. Always boiler.
B: Always the boiler! What do you do, sorry, I didn't ask.
A: Factory. Injection moulding. I run the machines, plastic packaging. Four days on, four days off.
B: Oh, so you don't do weekends like normal?
A: What do you mean exactly?
B: Sorry, I mean, like, is your weekend just whenever your four days off land?
A: Yes. I never know what day it is. Somebody says Saturday, I think, okay, maybe.
B: That sounds quite nice in a way, though? Like, four days off in a row.
A: First day I cook for whole week. Put in tubs. Then I walk, I fix bikes. I buy old bikes on Marketplace, fix, sell. Last one I pay twenty pounds, sell for ninety.
B: Ninety! That's actually really good. What was wrong with it?
A: Chain, brakes, tyres. Nothing difficult. People throw away things because they don't want to learn.
B: Yeah, that's true. My boyfriend's a sound technician, he's like that with speakers and stuff, he can't let anything go in the bin. Our flat's full of cables.
A: Is not bad.
B: No, it's not bad. Where are you from originally, if you don't mind me asking? Sorry.
A: Lithuania. Near Panevėžys. I am here sixteen years.
B: Oh wow. I'm from Kosovo, but I came when I was nine, so I sort of grew up here. Do you go back much?
A: Once, twice a year. Summer. From Luton.
B: Luton. Oh no.
A: Luton is a nightmare. But cheapest. I book four months before. Only small bag, nothing extra.
B: See, I'm the same, I do a whole shared note, flight times, everything. My family laugh at me. But when you go back it's not even a holiday, is it, it's just visiting everyone.
A: Yes. Mother, sister, her kids. Everybody wants you to eat.
B: Oh my God, yeah, that's exactly it. My nan doesn't let you leave the table.
A: Same.
B: Do you think you'd ever move back?
A: Mm. Maybe. I am saving for deposit. Here or there, I don't decide yet. Here, prices, you know. There, maybe I'm foreigner now also.
